title: Strata: cycle capacity provisioning and decision-gates for graceful scope pruning
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a repeatable framework (Strata) that provisions modular capacity tranches across cycles and codifies decision-gates for scope pruning. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle firefighting, make trade-offs explicit, and provide a predictable escalation path for critical work that needs surge resources.
background: We routinely experience mid-cycle pressure where emergent bugs, partner commitments, or priority shifts require fast reallocation of engineers. Current ad-hoc rebalances cause context-switch churn and untracked technical debt. Previous playbooks focus on headcount buffers or vague surge lanes but lack clear quantitative triggers and gate criteria for when to apply hard commits versus soft reserves.
goals: Define three capacity strata (Reserve, Elastic, Critical) with clear rules for assignment and release
Establish decision-gates tied to objective signals (SLO breach probability, blocker count, external commit)
Provide a lightweight cadence for manager approvals and cross-team trade-offs to limit context-switching
Produce a rollout template and runbook teams can adopt next cycle
proposal: Adopt a 'Strata' model: Reserve (5-10% soft buffer across squads), Elastic (role-based surge pool that can be temporarily assigned for up to two weeks), and Critical (hard-commit reserved capacity with contractual gating). Each stratum has a set of quantitative triggers and an approval flow: automated signal -> squad lead recommendation -> product PM assessment -> cycle capacity steward sign-off. Scope pruning is governed by a Scope Shepherd who owns a minimal viable checklist and final de-scoping authority when gates are met.
decision_gates: Gate A - Soft surge (Elastic): triggered when per-product median lead time for production fixes exceeds baseline by 30% OR when a high-severity customer issue is open >48hrs
Gate B - Hard-commit (Critical): triggered by a projected SLO breach probability >10% over 72 hours OR executive legal/compliance commitment with deadline in current cycle
Gate C - Release defer: used for cross-cycle reprioritization when combined velocity loss >15% if current scope is retained
rollout_plan: Pilot Strata in Cycle 2026-W10 with 3 squads (Console, Dedicated, Serving Runtime)
Run a tabletop exercise week 0 to validate signals and sign-off latency
Collect metrics during pilot: context-switch incidents, reopened tickets, sprint velocity delta
Iterate and publish a Strata template in Confluence and a one-click checklist in the Cycle kickoff doc
acceptance_criteria: Strata decision flow documented and accessible in Confluence with owner assignments
Pilot completed with data: one simulated Gate A and one real Gate B evaluation and recorded outcome
Cross-functional survey shows >=60% reduction in perceived mid-cycle disruption from participating squads
Template and runbook accepted by Eng leadership and PM council
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync with Eng leads and PM council. Aligned on the three strata vocabulary and initial percentage targets. Action: Marco to draft gate thresholds and data sources.

2026-02-20: Design reviewed the proposed user flows for Scope Shepherd approvals; suggested a 24-hour SLA for shepherd response and a lightweight mobile-friendly approval link. Action: DES to provide mockups for the Confluence checklist.

2026-02-24: Data team validated signals: SLO breach probability can be surfaced from the SLO service with 6-hour granularity; recommended smoothing window of 12 hours to reduce noise. Trade-off: longer smoothing reduces false positives but delays response.

2026-02-27: PM council requested explicit escalation path for customer escalations that bypass the normal gate when legal/contractual obligations are present. Decision: add 'executive override' with mandatory post-hoc retrospective.

2026-03-01: Draft playbook submitted for review. Requesting Eng leadership sign-off and a pilot commitment from Console, Dedicated, and Serving Runtime squads. Next step: tabletop exercise scheduling (owner Marco).
